title: Cross-SDK iterable pagination & batching helpers for embeddings + rerank with retry and streaming ergonomics
creator: Devon Liu
description: Goal: Provide a lightweight, consistent set of helper APIs across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that make it easy to: 1) page through large embedding/rerank responses, 2) batch requests for throughput-sensitive workloads, 3) apply robust retry/backoff policies for partial failures, and 4) consume streaming rerank/embeddings outputs with ergonomic iterators. Motivation: customers are building hybrid pipelines (embedding generation -> vector search -> reranking) and struggle with different SDK idioms, error handling, and pagination edge cases. This ticket scopes a cross-language design + reference implementation and example apps.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by SDK and Platform leads
Python/TS/Go helpers expose a common conceptual API (Iterator + BatchBuilder + RetryPolicy) with language-idiomatic wrappers
Helpers support server-side pagination tokens and client-side chunking with sane defaults; can compose with batching for throughput
Retry/backoff pluggable and defaults match platform SLOs (idempotency-aware where applicable)
Streaming rerank ergonomics: consumer can iterate partial results, pause/resume, and see stable offsets for checkpointing
Unit+integration tests covering: single/multi-page responses, transient failures with retries, streaming partial-close behavior
Documentation: examples in three languages and a migration snippet for existing customers
No regressions in existing embeddings/rerank SDK tests and CI passes in sdk-2026.03 branch
implementation_notes: Approach: implement a small core interface definition in the SDK design doc and then map to idiomatic constructs in each language (Python: generator + context manager; TS: async iterable plus helper class; Go: channel-style iterator with Close()). Prefer composition over inheritance. Keep helpers dependency-free aside from SDK client. Avoid changing core client surface; provide helpers in a separate utilities module so adoption is opt-in. Add feature flags behind experimental namespace for the initial rollout. Performance: ensure batching helper can accept an external BatchStrategy object so Dedicated users can plug in max-batch-size and total-token heuristics without SDK change. Ensure KV cache prefixing for rerank isn't inadvertently lost when batching requests. Telemetry: emit metric tags when helpers are used to track adoption and error rates (metric names: sdk.helper.pagination_used, sdk.helper.batch_retries).
api_sketch:
Python: from redwood_sdk.helpers import paginate_embeddings, batch_requests, RetryPolicy
Usage: for page in paginate_embeddings(client.generate_embeddings, queries, page_size=256, retry=RetryPolicy.defaults()): process(page)
TypeScript: const it = sdk.helpers.paginateEmbeddings(client.generateEmbeddings, queries, { pageSize: 256, retry: RetryPolicy.defaults() }); for await (const page of it) { /* ... */ }

Go: it := helpers.NewEmbeddingPager(client, queries, helpers.PageSize(256), helpers.DefaultRetryPolicy())
for page := range it.Pages() { /* handle page, check it.Err() after loop */ }

Batching helper: BatchBuilder takes an async/iterable of input items and emits batches sized by token-estimate or item-count threshold. Works as a pluggable utility for both embeddings and rerank calls.
RetryPolicy: backoff strategy, max_attempts, idempotency_hint. Default: exponential with jitter, max_attempts=3 for non-streaming, 5 for streaming-resume-capable endpoints.
test_plan: Unit tests per language covering: (a) single-page responses, (b) multi-page responses with server tokens, (c) transient 5xx then success (validate backoff and attempt counts), (d) streaming interruption and resume semantics, (e) batching edge cases (1 oversized item, variable token estimates). Integration: end-to-end example that runs embedding generation -> vector store mock -> rerank with pagination and batching. Load test: synthetic harness to validate that batching reduces per-token RPCs and does not increase tail latency beyond SLO. CI: add cross-lang smoke tests to SDK pipeline; gate feature behind experimental flag until rollout completes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): publish helpers as experimental module in Python/TS/Go with feature flag enabled in nightly packages; invite internal customers and Solutions Eng. Phase 2: collect telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate on ergonomics based on feedback. Phase 3: promote to stable in sdk-2026.03 and ship docs + migration guide. Provide opt-out toggles in hosted API for any behavior differences. Decommission experimental flag after 1 release cycle if no major issues.
